research_question: RQ2: is SDXL feasible on 8 GB VRAM at 512 px and at its native 1024 px?

config: fp16; DPMSolverMultistepScheduler; guidance 7.5; memory tier 0; no safety checker shipped; frozen kit c40749bc
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm_89, 8187.5 MiB)
peak_vram: 512x512: 7859.26 MiB allocated / 9030 MiB reserved / 8187.5 MiB device / 2309.61 MiB RSS. 1024x1024: 10738.08 MiB allocated / 14510 MiB reserved / 8187.5 MiB device / 6806.57 MiB RSS
evaluation: Human aggregate scores (1-5). Track A 512x512: 3/3/4/3/3/4/3 - IDENTICAL to SD 1.5 under the controlled condition. Track B native 1024x1024: prompt_adherence 4, style_consistency 5, visual_quality 5, decal_suitability 4, composition 4, artefacts 4, originality 3 - the visual-quality winner. Scored by Kylian at aggregate model/track level from complete contact-sheet rows, not per unit; per-unit cells are marked "not individually scored". reference_influence N/A (no reference image until Prototype 2); diversity_across_seeds NOT scored because the review sheets showed the fixed seed-42 comparison only - no value invented.
conclusion: Does NOT fit in 8 GB at native resolution, despite 30/30 runs reporting success - a result that would be misread without the memory figures. At 1024x1024 peak allocated (10738 MiB) and reserved (14510 MiB) both exceed the 8187.5 MiB of physical VRAM: Windows WDDM spilled silently into shared host memory (RSS 6807 MiB) instead of raising a CUDA OOM, so no exception was thrown and memory-tier escalation never triggered. Cost is roughly 29x SD 1.5 per 512 px image and about 118 s per native image. Even at 512 px it saturates the whole device. Separate factual observation: at 512 px it yields deck-shaped panels, but at its native 1024 px it yields FLAT artwork with no mockup framing - so the literal-deck reading seen in EXP-002 is resolution-dependent, not a property of all candidates. Judging both models only at 512 px would have mis-described SDXL, which is a direct vindication of the two-track design.
next_action: NOT selected as the production base model (DR-007): quality advantage exists only at a resolution this 8 GB GPU cannot hold. Retained as the visual-quality benchmark; revisit if a >=16 GB GPU becomes available.

research_question: RQ8: how should the ~1:3.6 deck aspect ratio be produced?
hypothesis: Direct tall generation degrades composition; generate-then-crop is more reliable
config: fp16; DPMSolverMultistepScheduler; guidance 7.5; memory tier 0; one strategy per fresh process; frozen kit c40749bc
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm_89, 8187.5 MiB)
peak_vram: 512x512 2675.38 MiB allocated; 512x1024 3283.69 MiB; 512x1536 3892.01 MiB; square-crop 2675.38 MiB (identical to 512x512, as expected)
duration: 512x512 median 4.111 s (spread 0.08); 512x1024 median 8.962 s (spread 0.09); 512x1536 median 15.244 s (spread 0.20); square-crop median 4.281 s (spread 0.53)
evaluation: Human aggregate scores (visual_quality / decal_suitability / composition). direct-1x1 4/2/3; direct-1x2 4/4/4; direct-1x3 4/5/4 (SELECTED); square-crop 3/2/3 (REJECTED as main strategy). Scored per strategy row, not per unit. Student findings: 1x1 too square and sometimes reads as a mockup; 1x2 balanced but does not fully use the deck ratio; 1x3 directly produces a tall decal reliably at ~3892 MiB, though some repetition or vertical stretching remains possible and must be addressed in later prompt, reference-conditioning and LoRA experiments; square-crop rejected because ~170x512 usable is far below deck-print resolution.
conclusion: 24/24 runs succeeded at tier 0. The hypothesis appears REFUTED on the memory and reliability axes: direct 1:3 generation reached 512x1536 in 3892 MiB, under half the VRAM budget, with no failures. square-crop's real cost is resolution - a 1:3 strip from 512x512 leaves only 170x512 usable pixels, far below deck-print needs. 1:3 is a stated approximation of the true ~1:3.6 because dimensions must be multiples of 64. Composition quality itself is Kylian's to judge. This experiment also produced a measurement-methodology correction: the first run put all four geometries in one process, which contaminated the reserved and device VRAM figures and inflated square-crop to 7.96 s for provably identical work. Thermal throttling was tested and RULED OUT (a hotter, more throttled card ran the same work faster, at 4.10 s); the cause was in-process caching-allocator state, and re-running one strategy per process cut timing spread about 20x.
next_action: SELECTED strategy: direct 1:3 generation at 512x1536 (DR-007). Adopt one-configuration-per-process for all VRAM/timing measurement in Prototypes 3-5.

config: Deck format only, medium level only (img2img strength 0.65, IP-Adapter scale 0.55); conditions C1, C2, C4; one fresh process per method because a different resolution is a different process
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (sm_89, 8187.5 MiB)
peak_vram: img2img 3892.01 MiB allocated - byte-identical to the text-only baseline, zero extra. ip-adapter 5140.69 MiB (+1248.68, the SAME fixed overhead as at 512x512) with PEAK DEVICE USED 7965.5 MiB of 8187.5 MiB physical - about 222 MiB spare, which is NOT to be described as comfortable headroom
duration: img2img median 7.980 s (fewer effective steps); ip-adapter median 12.022 s; text-only baseline 11.837 s
evaluation: 18/18 ok, tier 0, no overflow flag. Human aggregate: img2img 0.65 = originality 1 and copy risk 1, REJECTED as primary production mode; ip-adapter 0.55 = originality 4 and copy risk 4, visually usable and original. Failure probe: img2img C2/C4 worsen background_transfer (near-copy); ip-adapter C2/C4 REDUCE it but C4 worsens vertical_stretching and C1 worsens repeated_elements
conclusion: The hypothesis is CONFIRMED, and more sharply than expected. All six copy-risk flags in the entire milestone (dHash <= 6) are img2img at 512x1536 on the two references that are natively 512x1536, three of them at dHash 0-1 and perceptually indistinguishable from the reference. Median dHash for img2img at medium is 27 at 512x512 but 5 at 512x1536. Mechanism: img2img forces the reference into the output resolution, so when the aspect already matches nothing is cropped and denoising at 0.65 starts from an essentially intact copy. IP-Adapter shows no near-copy flag but is memory-critical here.
next_action: Decisive input to DR-008. A combined SD 1.5 + LoRA + IP-Adapter smoke test at 512x1536 is a mandatory acceptance item for the next relevant milestone (risk R12)
